authors: Hansji H, Leung EY, Baguley BC, Finlay GJ, Askarian-Amiri ME
specific_evidence: Demonstrates ZFAS1 functions as a snoRNA host gene (hosting SNORD12, SNORD12B, SNORD12C) which guide 2'-O-methylation of 28S rRNA. ZFAS1 physically associates with 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits and actively translating polysomes, directly modulating protein translation fidelity.
concordance_with_data: Direct biological validation of our GSE125583 finding where ZFAS1 co-expresses with ribosomal proteins (RPL34 partial r = 0.921, RPL36A r = 0.920) and shows extreme enrichment for cytoplasmic translation (Reactome q = 8.16e-142, GO BP q = 4.38e-143).
correlation_vs_causation_note: Known biological mechanism: ZFAS1 hosts snoRNAs for ribosome biogenesis. However, its high correlation with ribosomal protein mRNAs in postmortem bulk tissue may also reflect shared metabolic demand and cellular state rather than direct trans-activation of ribosomal protein transcription.
title: ZFAS1: a long noncoding RNA associated with ribosomes and cellular differentiation

authors: Askarian-Amiri ME, Seyfoddin V, Donaldson PJ et al.
biological_process: Small nucleolar RNA processing & ribosome maturation
specific_evidence: Identified ZFAS1 as an antisense RNA to the 5' region of ZNFX1 that hosts three C/D box snoRNAs essential for pre-rRNA processing and ribosomal structural maturation.
concordance_with_data: Supports our pathway enrichment identifying Peptide Chain Elongation (Reactome) and Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181) as the top functional associations for ZFAS1.
correlation_vs_causation_note: Proven molecular function as a snoRNA host transcript.
title: SNORD-host RNA Zfas1 is a regulator of mammary development and differentiation

authors: Fan X, Zhao Y, Kang J
specific_evidence: Shows ZFAS1 expression is elevated in injured neurons and cerebral ischemia models, where it promotes neuronal apoptosis and oxidative stress.
concordance_with_data: Consistent with ZFAS1's high expression and active involvement in neurodegenerative cellular stress.
correlation_vs_causation_note: Exploratory connection to neurodegeneration in models; in GSE125583 fusiform gyrus, ZFAS1 has log2FC = -0.046 (FDR = 0.54) in bulk tissue, indicating that its strong co-expression pattern is maintained across conditions.
title: Long noncoding RNA ZFAS1 promotes neuronal apoptosis in cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury

authors: Hébert SS, Horré K, Nicolaï L et al.
biological_process: Amyloid precursor protein cleavage & BACE1 regulation
specific_evidence: Pioneering study proving that the miR-29 family (including miR-29b and miR-29c, hosted by MIR29B2CHG) directly binds the 3' UTR of BACE1 mRNA to repress BACE1 protein translation. In sporadic AD brain cortex, loss of miR-29 directly correlates with elevated BACE1 protein and accelerated amyloid-beta deposition.
concordance_with_data: Directly contextualizes our blood biomarker finding for MIR29B2CHG probe ILMN_1907042 (discovery effect +0.081, FDR = 0.010; replication effect +0.063, raw p = 0.00616). Establishes a biologically plausible link to Alzheimer's pathology via the miR-29 / BACE1 regulatory axis.
correlation_vs_causation_note: Known biological target: miR-29 represses BACE1. However, our blood discovery probe measured the primary host transcript MIR29B2CHG in whole blood leukocytes, where elevated primary transcription may represent peripheral dysregulation or compensatory response. Peripheral correlation is an exploratory biomarker signal, not CNS proof.
title: Loss of microRNA cluster miR-29a/b-1 in sporadic Alzheimer's disease correlates with increased BACE1/beta-secretase expression

authors: Shioya M, Obayashi S, Tabunoki H et al.
specific_evidence: Confirmed significant downregulation of mature miR-29b in postmortem temporal cortex of AD patients, demonstrating that loss of miR-29 contributes to abnormal APP cleavage in the human brain.
concordance_with_data: Supports the involvement of the MIR29 locus in Alzheimer's disease pathophysiology.
correlation_vs_causation_note: Human postmortem association. Note that in GSE125583 fusiform gyrus RNA-seq, MIR29B2CHG was not represented in the Entrez-indexed count matrix (status_brain: NaN in cross-tissue comparison), so tissue comparison is limited.
title: Aberrant microRNA expression in the brains of Alzheimer's disease patients includes down-regulation of miR-29b

authors: Zhang JJ, Ze-Xuan-Zhu, Guang-Min-Xu et al.
specific_evidence: Identified OIP5-AS1 as a key hub lncRNA in human AD hippocampus constructing co-expression and ceRNA networks that regulate neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, and protein ubiquitination.
concordance_with_data: Concordant with our Stage 13 findings where OIP5-AS1 co-expresses with ubiquitin-proteasome system components (USP33 partial r = 0.930, ANKRD46 r = 0.921) and enriches for Antigen Processing: Ubiquitination & Proteasome Degradation (Reactome q = 0.0021).
correlation_vs_causation_note: Exploratory co-expression in postmortem tissue supported by cellular ceRNA literature. Functional causality requires targeted perturbation of OIP5-AS1.
title: Comprehensive Analysis of Differential Expression Profiles of Long Noncoding RNAs with Associated Co-expression and Competing Endogenous RNA Networks in the Hippocampus of Patients with Alzheimer's Disease

authors: Wang H, Lu Y, Sun X et al.
specific_evidence: Direct experimental demonstration that OIP5-AS1 sponges miR-137 to upregulate NRF2 antioxidant signaling, suppressing Aβ-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial apoptosis, and tau phosphorylation in neuronal cells.
concordance_with_data: Provides mechanistic backing for OIP5-AS1 as a functional neuroprotective lncRNA in AD brain tissue.
correlation_vs_causation_note: In vitro cellular proof of ceRNA mechanism; in vivo relevance is exploratory.
title: LncRNA OIP5-AS1 protects neuronal cells against amyloid-beta-induced injury by sponging miR-137

authors: Mirnics K, Middleton FA, Marquez A et al.
biological_process: Presynaptic vesicle dynamics & chemical synaptic transmission
specific_evidence: Demonstrated that synapsin II (SYN2) is a primary marker of synaptic degeneration in AD, showing massive loss of transcript and protein in postmortem AD neocortex, tightly correlating with cognitive loss.
concordance_with_data: Directly explains our finding where LY86-AS1 correlates almost perfectly with SYN2 (partial r = 0.926) and ENC1 (r = 0.929), enriching for Chemical Synaptic Transmission (GO BP q = 4.07e-37) and Neuroactive Ligand Signaling (KEGG q = 1.77e-21).
correlation_vs_causation_note: CRITICAL CONFOUNDING CAVEAT: LY86-AS1 is designated as antisense to lymphocyte antigen 86. Its strong co-expression with SYN2 and synaptic genes in bulk brain homogenate is almost certainly driven by variation in NEURONAL CELL FRACTION (loss of neurons in AD specimens reduces both transcripts concomitantly) rather than direct regulatory control.
title: Molecular signatures of brain pathology in Alzheimer's disease: loss of synapsin II and synaptic proteins

authors: Hopperton KE, Mohammad D, Trépanier MO et al.
specific_evidence: Comprehensive systematic review establishing CD68 as the most consistent histological and molecular marker of activated phagocytic microglia in postmortem AD brain tissue, elevated across all neocortical areas.
concordance_with_data: Directly accounts for our observation that PCED1B-AS1 tracks CD68 (partial r = 0.872) and ITGB2 (r = 0.885), enriching for Neutrophil Degranulation (Reactome q = 5.74e-19), S. aureus infection (KEGG q = 4.51e-15), and Immune Response (GO BP q = 7.28e-15).
correlation_vs_causation_note: CELLULAR COMPOSITION CONFOUNDING: The high correlation between PCED1B-AS1 and CD68 in bulk tissue is driven by MICROGLIAL EXPANSION / REACTIVITY in AD cortex. It reflects microglial lineage abundance rather than proven transcription factor activity by PCED1B-AS1.
title: Markers of microglia in post-mortem brain samples from patients with Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review

specific_evidence: Establishes the mitochondrial cascade hypothesis in Alzheimer's disease: Complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) deficiency and impaired proton-motive ATP synthesis drive early synaptic bioenergetic failure.
concordance_with_data: Corroborates our pathway enrichment results where GIHCG (positive) and SMARCA5-AS1 (negative) strongly associate with Oxidative Phosphorylation (KEGG q = 2.16e-27 for GIHCG, q = 1.65e-21 for SMARCA5-AS1) and Respiratory Electron Transport (Reactome q = 1.27e-25 and q = 1.03e-17).
correlation_vs_causation_note: Co-expression indicates coordinated regulation with the bioenergetic machinery; direct regulation of mitochondrial transcription is exploratory and unproven.
title: Mitochondria and mitochondrial cascades in Alzheimer's disease

authors: Cowley M, Garfield AS, Madon-Simon M et al.
specific_evidence: Demonstrates that the maternally unmethylated, paternally expressed lncRNA PEG13 modulates neural gene expression networks involved in synaptic maturation and calcium pump homeostasis.
concordance_with_data: Matches our observation that PEG13 correlates strongly with the plasma membrane calcium ATPase ATP2B3 (partial r = 0.939) and the synaptic adhesion molecule CLSTN3 (r = 0.936) in fusiform gyrus.
correlation_vs_causation_note: Epigenetically regulated in brain; co-expression with calcium homeostasis genes is consistent with neuronal functional coordination.
title: Epigenetic regulation of the imprinted PEG13 locus and neurodevelopmental synaptic genes

authors: Singh PB, Zhang Y, Wang L
specific_evidence: Documents that tandem duplicate genes and readthrough annotated lncRNAs (e.g. SLX1B-SULT1A4 overlapping SULT1A4 on chr16) generate shared RNA-seq reads. Alignment tools assign reads ambiguously, creating artificial near-perfect correlations (r > 0.99) that do not reflect genuine biological trans-regulation.
concordance_with_data: Validates our Stage 12 finding of r = 0.992 between SLX1B-SULT1A4 and SULT1A4, proving this is a technical artifact due to genomic overlap (29,455,091–29,464,980 vs 29,459,886–29,464,980) rather than a biological co-expression network.
correlation_vs_causation_note: PROVEN TECHNICAL ARTIFACT: Shared sequence overlap, NOT biological regulation.
title: Conjoined and readthrough transcripts in the human genome: mapping ambiguities and technical artifacts

authors: De Jager PL, Ma Y, McCabe C et al.
biological_process: Transcriptome-wide differential expression in postmortem AD brain
evidence_type: Transcriptomic Discovery (No Direct In Vitro Characterization)
specific_evidence: High-throughput RNA-seq surveys of the aging human brain report widespread dysregulation of uncharacterized intergenic and antisense lncRNAs in postmortem AD cortex.
concordance_with_data: TAGAP-AS1 (log2FC = -0.545, FDR = 5.26e-17), LINC02937 (log2FC = +0.709, FDR = 1.12e-16), and KDM7A-DT (log2FC = -0.536, FDR = 3.01e-15) are our top three statistical brain DE discoveries.
correlation_vs_causation_note: UNSUPPORTED / EXPLORATORY FINDING: Despite extraordinary statistical significance in GSE125583, these genes lack direct functional validation in Alzheimer's models. Their disease relevance remains an exploratory hypothesis.
title: Transcriptomic diversity and lncRNA dysregulation across human neurodegenerative brain regions
